references.text: Moses appointed leaders and officials over the tribes, just as Sukkot had its chiefs and elders who governed the city.
Moses wrote down the Lord's words, showing that writing was known and used in Israel, much like the young man in Sukkot could write down the names of the city's leaders.
Joshua wrote on stones, demonstrating that the Israelites mastered the art of writing, just as the young man from Sukkot could write.
Isaiah mentions that even a child can write, confirming that literacy was widespread in Israel, as seen when the young man in Sukkot wrote down the names of the leaders.
The context where Gideon first asked the men of Sukkot for help, and they refused to give food to his exhausted soldiers, leading to their judgment.
The fulfillment of Gideon's threat against the elders of Sukkot, using the list he had obtained written down by the young man.
